newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-IRAN'S ASIAN CUP HERO DREAMS OF WORLD CUP GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRAN'S ASIAN CUP HERO DREAMS OF WORLD CUP GLORY.

text.p: Striker Ali Daei is happy his seven-goal spree has taken triple-champions Iran to the verge of another Asian Cup final, but winning the title is not his dream.
What he really wants is to lead Iran into the World Cup.
''As a member of the Iranian national team, I wish I could go to and play at the World Cup,'' Daei told Reuters on Tuesday.
Iran has played only once in the World Cup -- back in 1978, when they were defeated by Peru and the Netherlands but earned an honourable draw against Scotland.

The 27-year-old stole the show at the Asian Cup on Monday with four goals in 22 minutes in Iran's stunning 6-2 quarter-final win over South Korea. He also scored in all Iran's three previous matches and is the tournament's leading goalscorer with seven.
Daei said he had expected Iran to beat South Korea but had not thought he would score four times against one of the tournament favourites.
''I and the team did well. I will try to do better in the coming matches and I hope we go on to win the tournament,'' he said, speaking through an interpreter in Abu Dhabi.
Scoring comes naturally to the six-foot-two- (189 cm-) tall striker.

He hit the net 12 times, including four goals in 12 minutes against Sri Lanka, to emerge as the most prolific striker in the Asian Cup's preliminary qualifiers, and was the top scorer in a regional tournament in Qatar two years ago.
He is dangerous in the air, has a natural instinct to be at the right place in the right time and possesses a lethal right foot.
Another of Daei's qualities is courage. In Iran's opening game against Iraq he suffered a cut over his left eye that required stitches.
But he came back on after treatment and was at the thick of the action, scoring his customary goal, this time from the penalty spot. He has been wearing a head-bandage during matches since.

Daei first kicked a ball at school in his home town Ardabil in northern Iran. He played for local teams until he caught the eye of one of Tehran's top clubs, Piroozi. He won local championships and cups with them before moving to Qatar last summer to sign for Saad Club.
Iran play Saudi Arabia in the semifinals on Wednesday. The teams met in the group stage last week when Iran emerged comfortable 3-0 winners with Daei grabbing a goal.
Asked whether he fancied his chances of repeating his feat Daei said: ''God willing (yes), but the important thing is that we beat them again.''
